summary: Per-card playtesting: N lane-agents, each with its own browser, tests a bucket of cards by tutoring each into hand and playing it.

notPlayed.notes: playSpell correctly NOT offered because 'Move an enemy unit' requires an enemy-unit target and none exist. Goldfish AI never plays units (cycled through turn 9 with zero opponent board), so no valid target could be produced in this environment. Card def has no explicit abilities field (relies on rulesText enrichment).

confirmed.what: 'I enter ready' not honored
confirmed.expected: Unit enters play ready (exhausted=false) and standardMove is immediately available
confirmed.observed: Entered with exhausted=true; no standardMove offered on the turn it was played. Card def (eager-drakehound.ts) is a stub with no entersReady/ability.
confirmed.reason: playUnit reducer sets exhausted=true unconditionally (cards.ts:526) with no enter-ready check. The card def stub (eager-drakehound.ts:4-15) has no abilities property, but runtime enrichment (enrich-cards.ts) parses rulesText into {type:"static", effect:{type:"enter-ready", target:"self"}} — verified by executing getAllCards(). However, nothing consumes it: trigger-matcher.ts:299 skips non-"triggered" abilities so play-self triggers ignore it; applyStaticEffect (static-abilities.ts:336-411) handles only modify-might/grant-keyword/grant-keywords, not enter-ready; and playUnit itself never queries checkReplacement or the enter-ready static. Thus the unit stays exhausted and standardMove enumerator filters it out (movement.ts:241). Note: the finding's "Layer: card" is debatable — the ability IS present at runtime via enrichment; the gap is engine-side (playUnit/static layer doesn't honor enter-ready statics). A card-layer fix would require re-typing the ability as a play-self triggered effect so effect-executor.ts:1148 fires.

confirmed.what: 'This enters exhausted' not honored
confirmed.expected: Gear enters play exhausted (exhausted=true), so its tap ability is unavailable on the turn it's played
confirmed.observed: Entered with exhausted=false; activateAbility was immediately offered. Card def (honeyfruit.ts) has no entersExhausted flag.
confirmed.reason: honeyfruit.ts:4-15 defines only rulesText — no `entersExhausted` flag and no `abilities` array implementing the static effect. The GearCard type (riftbound-types/src/cards/card-types.ts:210-222) has no `entersExhausted` field to set, and the playGear reducer (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:658-684) moves the card to base and fires triggers without ever setting the `exhausted` flag. Result: Honeyfruit enters ready and its [Exhaust]-costed activated ability is immediately usable, contrary to the printed "This enters exhausted."

confirmed.what: Activated ability grants wrong resources / Level 6 gate missing
confirmed.expected: At <6 XP only the base ability is usable, adding exactly 1 [rainbow] power (no energy). The [1][rainbow] variant is Level-6-gated.
confirmed.observed: Only one activateAbility (index 0) offered; activating it added +1 energy AND +1 rainbow power (energy 4→5, power {}→{rainbow:1}) at 0 XP. Rules-text auto-parser appears to have collapsed both [Add] lines into one ungated ability.
confirmed.reason: Runtime check (`getCardRegistry().get("unl-049-219").abilities`) returns a SINGLE activated ability: `{cost:{exhaust:true}, effect:{type:"add-resource", energy:1, power:["rainbow"]}, timing:"reaction", condition:{type:"while-level", threshold:6}}`. The base `[Add] [rainbow]` line is dropped; only the Level-6 variant survives (parser/index.ts ~3459-3499 add-match path). Engine side: `collectActivatedAbilities` (chain-moves.ts:292-391) and the `activateAbility` condition/enumerator (chain-moves.ts:598-935) never inspect `ability.condition`, so the `while-level:6` gate is ignored and the ability is offered at 0 XP. `executeEffect` case "add-resource" (effect-executor.ts:804-818) applies `energy:1` to `pool.energy` AND pushes `rainbow` into `pool.power`, yielding exactly the observed +1 energy and +1 rainbow. All three observed sub-claims (single index-0 ability, energy+rainbow granted, no Level-6 gate) reproduce from source.

confirmed.what: Deathknell — Channel 1 rune exhausted did not fire on death
confirmed.expected: When the unit dies, controller channels 1 rune from rune deck into rune pool, entering exhausted (rune count 2→3)
confirmed.observed: Killed via Bellows Breath (1 dmg → trash). Rune pool stayed at 2 ready runes; no new rune channeled, no chain trigger, no pendingChoice. Card def (soaring-scout.ts) is a stub with no abilities.
confirmed.reason: soaring-scout.ts:4-15 defines ogn-216-298 with rulesText "[Deathknell] — Channel 1 rune exhausted" but no `abilities` field. The engine reads `abilities`, not rulesText (per watchful-sentry.ts:5-6 comment referencing Rule 808.1, and keyword-effects.ts:68 which registers Deathknell as a keyword ability requiring an explicit `{keyword: "Deathknell", effect: ...}` entry). With no abilities array, the death event dispatcher finds no listener for this card, so no channel effect fires and rune pool stays at 2. Compare working sibling watchful-sentry.ts:7-13 which declares the abilities array.

confirmed.what: Spell-cost discount for spells choosing Irelia not applied
confirmed.expected: Casting Bellows Breath (base cost 1) targeting Irelia costs 0 energy ([1] or [rainbow] less)
confirmed.observed: Energy went 9→8 (full 1 paid). Card def declares a static 'ChooseSelfCostReduction' keyword with a code comment noting engine support is 'still pending'.
confirmed.reason: Irelia (sfd-141-221) declares its discount as a static grant-keyword effect with keyword "ChooseSelfCostReduction" (irelia-graceful.ts:14-22), and the card-def comment at lines 10-11 explicitly states engine support is "still pending". Grep confirms "ChooseSelfCostReduction" appears nowhere in riftbound-engine. The cost-deduction path (cards.ts deductCost, lines 246-279) computes adjustedEnergy from base cost + costModifier − interactive reduction only; getInteractiveReduction (cards.ts:121-135) handles only the "target-might" mode on the PLAYED card, not keywords on the chosen target. The board-scan reducer computeStaticCostReduction filters strictly on effect.type === "cost-reduction" (static-cost-reduction.ts:149), so Irelia's grant-keyword ability is skipped. Result: casting a 1-cost spell (Bellows Breath) targeting Irelia deducts the full 1 energy — 9→8, matching the observed behavior.

confirmed.what: Additional cost 'kill a friendly unit' not paid; no resurrection effect
confirmed.expected: On cast: the chosen friendly unit (Enthralling Protector) is killed as part of the cost, then a prompt to play a unit from trash costing ≤ its cost is shown
confirmed.observed: Spell cast for 2 energy with Protector as target; after chain resolution Protector is still alive in base, trash contains only the spell itself, no pendingChoice/prompt shown. Card def (heedless-resurrection.ts) is a stub with no additionalCost or effect.
confirmed.reason: heedless-resurrection.ts:4-16 defines the SpellCard with no `abilities` field at all — no additionalCost.kill and no effect. Contrast sacrifice.ts (unl-173-219) which correctly wires `abilities: [{ additionalCost: { kill: {...} }, effect: {...} }]`. With no abilities, the engine's additionalCost pipeline (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts, effect-executor.ts) never runs, so casting just pays 2 energy and trashes the spell — the targeted friendly unit is never killed and no play-from-trash prompt is generated.

confirmed.what: On-play 'play a spell from your trash' trigger resolves with no effect
confirmed.expected: After playing Fizz with Retreat (cost 1 spell) in trash: a pendingChoice prompt to optionally play Retreat from trash (ignoring energy cost), then recycle it to bottom of deck
confirmed.observed: Trigger did go on chain as {type:'play', from:'trash', target:{type:'spell'}} but on resolution: no pendingChoice, no spell played, Retreat still in trash (trash stayed 1), deck size unchanged (no recycle). Also no cost≤3 filter or 'may' in the chain payload. Card def is a stub; auto-parsed effect is a no-op in the resolver.
confirmed.reason: Runtime parser (enrich-cards.ts:29 → parseAbilities) yields exactly {type:'play', from:'trash', target:{type:'spell'}, optional:true} for Fizz's rulesText — verified by executing parseAbilities. On chain resolution (chain-moves.ts:188-220), resolveTarget({type:'spell', quantity:'all'}) is called: target-resolver.ts:64 only enumerates getBoardCardIds (base+battlefields, never trash), and type:'spell' matches none of the unit/gear/equipment/permanent filters, so options=[] after excluding self → boundTargets=[]. The 'play' handler at effect-executor.ts:1052-1064 reads `from` but never uses it, iterates the empty target list, and does nothing — no pendingChoice, no cost≤3 filter, no recycle. Card def fizz-trickster.ts:4-18 is a stub (no abilities field). Report's Observed matches exactly.

confirmed.what: Spell effect not implemented — no target selection, no might doubling, no ability grant
confirmed.expected: Prompt to choose a unit; on resolution that unit's Might is doubled and it gains an activated '[rainbow][rainbow]: Ready me' ability for the turn
confirmed.observed: playSpell offered with no targets param; chain item had effect.type='raw' with the literal rules text; after resolution the only unit in play (Noxian Drummer) still had might=3 (unchanged) and no new activateAbility was enumerated for it
confirmed.reason: ven-142-166 (Dominus) has no hand-authored TS definition (no /packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ven/ dir, no grep hits for "ven-142" in *.ts). Its ven.json entry has abilities:[null], which adaptJsonCard (all-cards.ts:805-807) maps to undefined so enrichCard (enrich-cards.ts:29) reparses rulesText. Running parseAbilities on the exact rulesText yields {type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:{type:"raw", text:"This turn, double a unit's Might and give it..."}} — no target descriptor and an unstructured effect. The playSpell enumerator (cards.ts:759-760) finds a spell ability with no effect.target so offers no targets param, and on resolution effect-executor.ts:319-1318 has no case for "raw" (nor "double-might" nor any grant-activated-ability case) — the default at effect-executor.ts:1316 is `break`, a no-op. Result: no target prompt, no might doubling, no granted "[rainbow][rainbow]: Ready me" ability — matches the observed behavior exactly.

confirmed.what: Gold gear tokens created NOT exhausted
confirmed.expected: rulesText: 'play two Gold gear tokens exhausted' — both tokens should have meta.exhausted=true
confirmed.observed: Both tokens created with meta.exhausted=false
confirmed.reason: sfd-152-221 (Eminent Benefactor, eminent-benefactor.ts:13) has only rulesText "When I hold, play two Gold gear tokens exhausted." — no hand-authored abilities, so it goes through the parser. The gear-token parser at riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:1964-1985 matches `(exhausted)?` as capture group 4 but never reads gearMatch[4]; the emitted CreateTokenEffect contains only {type:"create-token", token:{name:"Gold",type:"gear"}, amount:2} with no exhausted flag. The engine's create-token handler at effect-executor.ts:868-898 then loops `ctx.createCardInZone(tokenId, targetZone, ctx.playerId)` and registers the card def, but never calls counters.setFlag(..., "exhausted", true) or updateCardMeta on the new token. Core createCardInZone (core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:40) does not initialize cardMetas for the new card. Net effect: both Gold tokens enter play ready (meta.exhausted absent/falsy), not exhausted, contradicting the rules text.

confirmed.what: Gold tokens have cardType 'unknown' instead of 'gear'
confirmed.expected: Tokens are gear (rulesText says 'Gold gear tokens'); cardType should be 'gear' so gear-referencing effects/zones treat them correctly
confirmed.observed: cardType='unknown', definitionId='token-gold-<timestamp>-N' (not a registered def)
confirmed.reason: effect-executor.ts:888 mints tokenId `token-gold-${Date.now()}-${i}` and registers it (with cardType 'gear') only in the engine's runtime getGlobalCardRegistry(); chain-moves.ts:99 sets the core card instance's definitionId to that same tokenId. server.ts:114 instead uses the static riftbound-cards Map from getCardRegistry() (all-cards.ts:844), so at server.ts:651 registry.get('token-gold-<ts>-N') returns undefined and server.ts:661 emits cardType: 'unknown'. Matches observed definitionId format and cardType.

confirmed.what: Gold token name/render shows internal id instead of 'Gold'
confirmed.expected: Token displays as a Gold gear card with name 'Gold'
confirmed.observed: UI renders placeholder card labelled 'token-gold-1785896502043-0 / UNKNOWN' in the base row
confirmed.reason: Registry mismatch: effect-executor.ts:886-896 creates the Gold token with instance id `token-gold-{Date.now()}-{i}` (line 888), sets that same string as the card's definitionId via the chain-moves.ts:99 wrapper, and registers {name:"Gold", cardType:"gear"} into the engine's getGlobalCardRegistry() (CardDefinitionRegistry). But the server snapshot builder uses a completely separate static registry — server.ts:114 `const registry = getCardRegistry()` returns a plain Map<string,Card> built once from getAllCards() (all-cards.ts:844-849). At server.ts:651 `registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId)` looks up "token-gold-1785896502043-0" in that static Map, misses, so def=undefined; server.ts:661 emits cardType:"unknown" and server.ts:669 emits name:cardId. renderer.js:691/770 then displays the raw id as the card name with cardType "unknown" → the observed "token-gold-1785896502043-0 / UNKNOWN" placeholder instead of "Gold" gear.

confirmed.what: Static 'Your spells and abilities deal 1 Bonus Damage' not applied
confirmed.expected: With Annie in play, casting Falling Star (Deal 3 to a unit) should deal 4 damage to the target
confirmed.observed: Target (Annie herself, might 4) took meta.damage=3 and survived; chain item effect.amount was 3; no +1 applied on resolution
confirmed.reason: Annie (ogs-001-024) encodes her static as a grant-keyword effect {keyword:"BonusDamage", target:"controller", value:1} (annie-fiery.ts:15-25), and static-abilities.ts:357-387 writes that into grantedKeywords meta. But the spell/ability damage pipeline never reads it: effect-executor.ts case "damage" (lines 375-427) resolves `amount` straight from effect.amount (376-380), only checks `type:"take-damage"` replacements (393-394) — not "deals-bonus-damage" — and applies the raw `amount` to counters/meta (418-424) with no BonusDamage lookup. A grep of the engine (non-test) for "BonusDamage" returns zero hits; no grantedKeywords consumer (hunt-keyword.ts, combat.ts, movement.ts, damage-requirements.ts, etc.) handles that keyword. So Falling Star's 3 stays 3 and Annie (might 4) survives with meta.damage=3. The card file comment even concedes "support is partial today" (annie-fiery.ts:13).

confirmed.what: Deathknell 'Recycle me to ready your runes' did not trigger
confirmed.expected: When Ekko dies, a triggered ability goes on chain; on finalization the cost 'recycle me' moves Ekko to bottom of deck and all controller's runes ready (rule 383.3.b explicitly cites this card)
confirmed.observed: Ekko took 5 damage (might 5) and went straight to trash; no chain item was queued; the previously-exhausted Mind Rune stayed exhausted
confirmed.reason: Ekko's parsed ability is `{type:"keyword", keyword:"Deathknell", effect:{…}}` (verified by running `parseAbilities` on its rulesText via enrichCards). `toTriggerableAbilities` (trigger-runner.ts:80) only accepts `a.type === "triggered" && a.trigger`, so the Deathknell keyword ability is dropped and the function returns `[]` for Ekko (verified empirically). `findMatchingTriggers` (trigger-matcher.ts:299) has the same `type !== "triggered"` skip. Consequently `dispatchUnitDied` → `dispatchEvent` → `fireTriggers` finds zero matches on the `die` event and never calls `addToChain` (trigger-runner.ts:296-322), so no chain item is queued and the exhausted runes are never readied. The synthesis claimed in listener-registry.ts:8-10 ("Deathknell and Legion keywords are synthesised into real triggered abilities") does not exist anywhere in the engine — no code converts `keyword:"Deathknell"` into a `{type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"die", on:"self"}}` shape.

confirmed.what: Accelerate optional cost not offered
confirmed.expected: With energy≥1 and mind power≥1 available, playing Ekko should offer paying [1][mind] extra to enter ready (either as a separate move variant or a pendingChoice prompt)
confirmed.observed: Only a single playUnit move enumerated with no accelerate param; no pendingChoice on play; Ekko entered exhausted and the 1 mind power was not spent
confirmed.reason: playUnit has no Accelerate wiring. Enumerator (lines 497-513) emits exactly one `{cardId, location:"base", playerId}` per affordable unit — no accelerate/paidAdditionalCost variant. Reducer unconditionally sets exhausted at line 526 (`counters.setFlag(cardId, "exhausted", true)`) and hardcodes `paidAdditionalCost: false` at line 536, with the inline comment at 532-534 admitting "optional-cost enumeration is not wired into playUnit". No pendingChoice is created. `shouldEnterReady` (keyword-effects.ts:329) is dead code — grep shows zero references anywhere under game-definition/ or abilities/. Ekko (ogn-110-298) has Accelerate only in rulesText; there is no engine path to offer or pay the [1][mind] optional cost.

confirmed.what: Spell resolves with no effect — no target prompt, target unit not readied, no Assault 3 granted
confirmed.expected: On resolution, prompt to choose a unit, ready that unit, and grant it Assault 3 for the turn
confirmed.observed: Played spell with an exhausted Watchful Sentry on board; spell went on chain, resolved after passChainPriority, went to trash. Sentry remained exhausted:true, might:1. No pendingChoice, no chain effect payload. Card has no .ts impl (no ven/ dir) and JSON abilities=[], parseSuccess=false.
confirmed.reason: ven-012-166 (Perfect Execution) has "abilities": [] and "parseSuccess": false at ven.json:670-671 despite rulesText "Ready a unit and give it [Assault 3] this turn". No .ts implementation exists — /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/index.ts:8-11 exports only ogn/ogs/sfd/unl (no ven/ directory). Registry.getAbilities (card-lookup.ts:162-164) returns the empty array; playSpell reducer (cards.ts:895-897) then finds no spellAbility, so effect stored on the chain is undefined. The spell resolves as a no-op: no target prompt, target not readied, no Assault 3 granted — exactly as observed.

confirmed.what: Karthus's passive ('Your Deathknell effects trigger an additional time') is not implemented
confirmed.expected: With Karthus in play, killing Watchful Sentry (Deathknell — Draw 1) should draw 2 cards
confirmed.observed: Karthus + Watchful Sentry both at base; cast Vengeance on Sentry; Sentry moved to trash but hand size unchanged (5→5). karthus-eternal.ts has no abilities array.
confirmed.reason: karthus-eternal.ts defines only rulesText with no `abilities` array, and per watchful-sentry.ts:5-6 the engine reads `abilities` not rulesText. The parser emits a `type: "trigger-double"` effect (static-parser.ts:1111) but that string appears nowhere in riftbound-engine/src/ — no dispatcher, listener-registry, or effect handler consumes it. ogn.json:8540-8549 mis-parsed the text as an empty-sequence Deathknell keyword, which is also a no-op. So Karthus's Deathknell-doubling passive has zero runtime implementation; killing Watchful Sentry with Karthus in play draws 1, not 2.

confirmed.what: 'When you play me to a battlefield' trigger fires when played to base
confirmed.expected: Trigger should only fire when the unit is played directly to a battlefield location, not to base
confirmed.observed: Only playUnit location=base was offered; after playing to base, chain contained a triggered ability {type:'damage', amount:2, target:{controller:'enemy', location:'here'}}. Screenshot shows Chain modal with 'Mischievous Marai — ability' after playing to base.
confirmed.reason: The trigger pattern `{ event: "play-self", pattern: /^When you play (?:me|this)(?:\s+to a battlefield)?,\s*/i }` at parser/index.ts:3669 consumes "to a battlefield" as an optional non-capturing group but emits a bare `{event: "play-self", on: "self"}` trigger with NO `self-at-battlefield` restriction. This is confirmed by the generated data at riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/unl.json (unl-003-219 trigger is `{event: "play-self", on: "self"}`, no restrictions). The engine's trigger-matcher.ts:132-133 does implement a `self-at-battlefield` restriction check (`card.zone.startsWith("battlefield")`), but since the parser never emits it for this pattern, `triggerMatchesEvent` returns true when `card.zone === "base"` (findMatchingTriggers at trigger-matcher.ts:291 allows zone `"base"`). Per rule 383.2.a.1, "to a battlefield" is part of the trigger condition and must gate placement on the chain — so firing at base is incorrect. Fix: split the pattern so the "to a battlefield" variant emits `restrictions: [{type: "self-at-battlefield"}]` (as done for the Vex pattern at parser/index.ts:3947).

confirmed.what: Spell effect is 'move friendly unit to base' — wrong destination and missing the other two clauses
confirmed.expected: Prompt to choose a destination for the friendly unit (a battlefield), then optionally attach an Equipment with same controller, then grant that unit 'When I conquer, you may move me to my base' for the turn
confirmed.observed: Chain effect was {type:'move', to:'base', target:{controller:'friendly', type:'unit'}}. Targeted Trusty Ramhound already at base; on resolution nothing changed — unit stayed at base, no destination choice, no equipment attach prompt, no granted ability. relentless-pursuit.ts has no abilities/effect definition.
confirmed.reason: relentless-pursuit.ts:4-16 declares no abilities/effect field, so enrich-cards.ts:29 falls through to parseAbilities(rulesText). Running getCardRegistry().get("sfd-184-221") via bun yields exactly abilities[0].effect = {type:"move", to:"base", target:{type:"unit", controller:"friendly"}} — matching the report's observed chain effect. Root cause of to:"base": parser/index.ts:1093-1137 (basicMatch) matches "Move a friendly unit." with destStr undefined and line 1131 defaults `to = "base"` instead of "choose"; the second/third sentences (Equipment attach, grant "When I conquer…") produce no additional effects. At resolution, effect-executor.ts:544-583 with dest==="base" skips the choose-destination pendingChoice branch (549-567) and just calls zones.moveCard({targetZoneId:"base"}) — no destination prompt, no equipment-attach prompt, no ability grant; a unit already at base is a no-op.

confirmed.what: Move trigger fires but resolution has no observable effect — no reveal shown, no draw, no recycle logged
confirmed.expected: On move, reveal the top card of Main Deck to both players; if it's a gear, add it to hand; otherwise put it on the bottom of the deck. Game log should record the reveal.
confirmed.observed: standardMove put trigger on chain with effect {type:'reveal', from:'deck', amount:1, until:'gear', then:{type:'recycle', from:'board', amount:1}}. After passChainPriority: hand size unchanged (6→6), trash unchanged (0→0), deck count unchanged (34→34), no reveal UI shown, no game-log entry for reveal or recycle.
confirmed.reason: The card def (apprentice-smith.ts:15-27) correctly creates a triggered ability with effect {type:'reveal', from:'deck', amount:1, until:'gear', then:{type:'recycle',...}}. However, the effect executor's `case "reveal":` at effect-executor.ts:1072-1075 is a stub — it contains only a comment "Reveal cards — informational only for now" and `break;`. It performs no zone read, no narrator/game-log emit, no gear check, no draw, and does not process the `then` clause (generic `then` handling only exists in the conditional branch at line ~940, not for `reveal`). So the trigger goes on the chain and resolves, but resolution is a no-op — matching the observed hand 6→6, deck 34→34, trash 0→0, no reveal UI, no log entry.

confirmed.what: 'I enter ready' replacement effect not applied
confirmed.expected: Unit enters play ready (exhausted:false), unlike normal units which enter exhausted
confirmed.observed: After playUnit, state shows exhausted:true — same as a control unit (Honest Broker) played immediately after. Screenshot /tmp/card-ogs-016-024-played.png shows the card tapped in base.
confirmed.reason: playUnit reducer unconditionally sets exhausted:true (cards.ts:526) with no enters-ready replacement check — grep shows zero references to checkReplacement or "enters-ready" anywhere in game-definition/, despite replacement-effects.ts:39 declaring "enters-ready" as a supported event. Additionally, the card def (vanguard-attendant.ts:4-15) has no abilities field (only rulesText), and card-lookup.ts:163 reads abilities solely from def.abilities, so registry.getAbilities("ogs-016-024") returns []. Even if abilities were present, the parser emits type:"static" (static-parser.ts:953) not type:"replacement", which checkReplacement (replacement-effects.ts:261) would skip. Net: ogs-016-024 enters exhausted exactly like a vanilla unit.

confirmed.what: 'When you use an activated ability of a gear, give me +1 [Might] this turn' never triggers
confirmed.expected: After activating Orb of Regret's [Exhaust] ability with Prize of Progress on board, a trigger goes on the chain and Prize's might becomes 4 (base 3 +1) for the turn
confirmed.observed: Activated Orb of Regret (gear exhausted:true, its ability appeared alone on the chain and resolved). No Prize-of-Progress trigger was ever added to the chain and Prize's might stayed at 3 through resolution. Screenshot /tmp/card-sfd-075-221-final.png.
confirmed.reason: The parser emits trigger event "use-activated-ability" (parser/index.ts:3840) for Prize of Progress, but the engine never fires that event: the activateAbility reducer (chain-moves.ts:934-1000) contains no fireTriggers call (the only fireTriggers calls in that file are at lines 105/233/248/252, all in spell/choose resolution paths), and the GameEvent union (game-events.ts:11-36) has no "use-activated-ability" variant. A repo-wide grep confirms parser/index.ts:3840 is the sole occurrence of that string. So no event ever matches the trigger and Prize's might stays at base 3.

confirmed.what: 'When you play a spell, give me +1 Might' trigger resolves without applying the +1
confirmed.expected: After each spell cast, Ravenbloom Student's effective might increases by 1 (mightModifier increments)
confirmed.observed: Trigger goes on chain with effect {type:modify-might,amount:1,target:'self',duration:'turn'} and resolves, but meta.mightModifier does not change. After casting En Garde (+2) then Meditation (no might), mightModifier stayed at 2 (expected 4). Second spell alone: 2→2 (expected 2→3).
confirmed.reason: ogn-103-298's rulesText is parsed by enrichCards (the .ts def has no abilities), producing effect {type:'modify-might', amount:1, target:'self', duration:'turn'} — target is the STRING 'self', not {type:'self'} (verified via bun repro). fireTriggers (trigger-runner.ts:306-321) puts this on the chain with no bound targets. In executeResolvedItem (chain-moves.ts:189-220), line 189 casts effect.target to TargetDescriptor and line 193 checks `target.type !== "self"` — but ('self' as string).type is undefined, so the guard passes and the code enters the choose-target branch. It then calls resolveTarget({...'self', quantity:'all'}) which spreads to {0:'s',1:'e',2:'l',3:'f',quantity:'all'}; resolveTarget treats this as an object with undefined type, collects all board cards, and at target-resolver.ts:150-152 EXCLUDES sourceCardId (Ravenbloom) because target.type !== 'self'. The resulting options never include Ravenbloom: with 0 other cards boundTargets=[], with 1 it targets the wrong card, with ≥2 it opens a pendingChoice. In every case getTargetIds (effect-executor.ts:119) returns ctx.boundTargets instead of resolving 'self', so the modify-might loop at effect-executor.ts:638-649 never touches Ravenbloom's meta.mightModifier. Matches observed 2→2 after each spell trigger.

confirmed.what: 'When I conquer' trigger does not fire — no Shadow Clone token created
confirmed.expected: After Zed conquers a battlefield, a 0-Might Shadow Clone unit token appears in player-1 base and a chain item is created
confirmed.observed: Zed conquered Aspirant's Climb (VP went 0→1) but base remained empty, interaction.nextChainItemId stayed at 1 (no ability ever chained), no token anywhere in zones
confirmed.reason: Observed behavior reproduces: after Zed moves to an open battlefield and both players pass the non-combat showdown, VP goes 0→1 but no conquer trigger is chained. Root cause is engine-layer, not card-layer: the passShowdownFocus reducer's non-combat-showdown close block (chain-moves.ts:1063-1086) sets bf.controller and awards the VP (line 1072) but never calls fireTriggers({type:"conquer", playerId, battlefieldId}, ...). The alternate conquerBattlefield move (combat.ts:667, which does call fireTriggers) is unreachable afterward because its condition returns false once bf.controller === playerId (combat.ts:561-563). The card itself is fine — ven.json's abilities:[null] is filtered by adaptJsonCard (all-cards.ts:805-807), enrichCard re-parses rulesText into a valid {type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"conquer", on:"self"}, effect:{type:"create-token", token:{name:"Shadow Clone",...}}}, and findMatchingTriggers correctly matches it against a conquer event (verified by direct execution: fireTriggers pushed a chain item and nextChainItemId went 1→2).
